A long long time ago, when Manchester United was a genuinely successful football club, a group of researchers wondered whether being a fan of the team would affect someone’s willingness to help a supporter of a rival outfit. Their experiment can teach managers something about group identities at work, the subject of this week’s Bartleby column.   And my weekly newsletter for subscribers looks at a paper that asks why meetings are both so disliked and so persistent. Broccoli supplies the answer. You can sign up to read that here.   Andrew Palmer, Bartleby columnist Latest column Are you committed to your company or your team? Employees have overlapping identities at work. That’s a challenge for bosses Humans are conditioned to form allegiances extremely quickly, a type of behaviour sometimes called the “minimal group effect”. In a famous series of experiments, a social psychologist called Henri Tajfel found that you can divide strangers into groups on totally arbitrary grounds—how good they are at estimating the number of dots on a chart, say, or how much they like a certain type of abstract art, or even just on the basis of a coin toss—and they will immediately start to favour members of their own group when then asked to distribute rewards. From the Boss Class vault Innovation: Coming up with new ideas Forget the whiteboards, hammocks and ping-pong tables How do the world’s biggest firms develop their best ideas? At Google, whose flagship product is threatened by artificial intelligence, that question is urgent. Liz Reid’s job is to find the answer. On our “Boss Class” podcast the tech giant’s head of search explains how she develops ideas. Elsewhere in The Economist ▸ Should Anthropic press pause on a potential $2trn IPO? ▸ The new age of the orator ▸ Are teenagers growing dimmer? Enjoying this newsletter? If you’re a subscriber you can get it in your inbox every Monday by signing up here. You’ll get more on work and office life from our management columnist.

79091.subject: Pump Strikes Back
79091.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/eaa70932-7ce4-467e-b338-a662ed575d6a/0xR_NL_Banner_Heading_Wordmark.jpg?t=1776775276)
Caption: 

Happy Monday. Every major benchmark closed the week lower as hot core CPI and $100 oil pushed the odds of a hike at this week's Fed meeting to 87%, Trump signed off on an ethics provision that gives the Clarity Act its best odds since July, and on Solana a launchpad that matched Pump.fun's revenue in a week got its best features copied the next week. 

In today's edition, we discuss the sell-off into the Fed decision and the fight between StonkFun and Pump.fun.

———————————————————————————

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/42e942ec-f31d-4957-8722-a3ac7b121e1e/0xR_NL_Market_Update.png?t=1767631151) [Market Update]
Caption: 

All four major benchmarks finished the week in the red. The S&P 500 fell 1.4%, while the Nasdaq and gold both declined 2.4%. BTC was the weakest performer, ending the week down 4.5%.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/30c3b98f-fda5-4537-9000-04c7f0c3dbe6/image.png?t=1789378893)
Caption: 

As covered in Friday’s [edition](https://blockworks.com/newsletter/0xresearch), the sell-off has been driven by rising expectations for further rate hikes. Core CPI increased 0.3% MoM, above expectations, while WTI continues to trade around $100. Markets now [price](https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html) an 86.7% chance of a hike at this week’s Fed meeting and a 25% chance of three hikes by the end of 2026.

The major crypto [news](https://apnews.com/article/donald-trump-cryptocurrency-ethics-521fd5986eb107413064018f7a468c51) this morning is that Trump has agreed to a new bipartisan ethics provision in the proposed Clarity Act, which is heading for a key vote this week. The revised rules would allow state attorneys general to enforce restrictions preventing federal officials from issuing, sponsoring or holding significant interests in digital assets. They could also act against exchanges that list assets in violation of those restrictions.

The development has pushed the odds of the Clarity Act becoming law in 2026 to [32%](https://polymarket.com/event/clarity-act-signed-into-law-in-2026), their highest level since late July. For anyone wondering what the bill could mean for the digital asset industry, I could not recommend this [read](https://app.blockworksresearch.com/research/how-clarity-reshapes-crypto-regulation) more.

The weakness extended across crypto, with every sector we track finishing the week deep in the red except Gaming, which ended roughly flat.
